passage: Nirmala's face burned all Monday. She had spilled ink across Aparna's storybook, and part of her felt like a bad person, until she saw that she had done a bad thing, and bad things can be mended. "I am sorry I spoiled your book," she said. "Can I buy you a new one with my savings?" Aparna nodded and smiled. That evening Nirmala confessed to her mother, Jasleen, who hugged her at once. "I am glad you told me. Everyone slips, and this can be put right." Nirmala felt a weight lift. On Friday, at the annual day, she tripped over the hem of her costume and stammered through her line, and the whole hall laughed. She wanted to vanish through the stage floor. Behind the curtain, Aparna slid in next to her. "I will walk out with you," Aparna said. "Nobody is thinking about it." By recess the talk had moved on to the snack stall.

qa.q: What did Nirmala spill on Aparna's storybook?
qa.a: She spilled ink on it.

qa.q: How did Nirmala's shame over the ink differ from her feelings after the hall laughed, and what helped each?
qa.a: After the ink she said she was sorry and offered to buy a new book with her savings, which mended it, but nothing could mend the whole hall laughing, so what helped was Aparna slipping in next to her behind the curtain and walking out with her.

qa.q: How did Nirmala feel when her mother hugged her at once?
qa.a: She felt relieved, as if a weight had lifted.

qa.q: What could Nirmala do next time she makes a mistake?
qa.a: She could apologise and offer to fix it, and tell her mother soon, as she did about the ink.

grounding: A child's three moments of shame: guilt over spoiled ink that she mends, a mother's quick forgiveness, and the laughter of a whole hall softened by a friend's company.

passage: Sumit's post glittered: trading profits, a new car, a caption about freedom. Tanvir felt left behind, and remembered his own losses from the spring, when he had put his savings into a hot tip and hidden it from everyone, feeling stupid. Then a creator's video flashed a countdown timer and screenshots of gains. "Only two hours left!" His pulse rose. He closed the app, told himself that anything which must be decided today was not for him, and slept on it. Next morning his partner Siddharth, who had noticed the odd late-night trades, said quietly, "I am scared about the risky bets, and I don't know what you hold." Tanvir wanted to defend himself, but instead he showed Siddharth every holding and confessed the spring loss. They agreed on a small limit for experiments, and Tanvir wrote down his rules: no tips, and a review each month. Later he noticed that Sumit's page never showed a single loss, and he compared his savings to last year's, not to the car.

qa.q: What did the creator's video use to create urgency?
qa.a: It used a countdown timer and screenshots of gains.

qa.q: How did Tanvir's handling of the creator's countdown differ from his earlier hot tip?
qa.a: Earlier he put his savings into a hot tip and hid the loss, feeling stupid, but with the countdown he closed the app, told himself anything that must be decided today was not for him, and slept on it.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling about Tanvir's late-night trades?
qa.a: Siddharth was scared, saying he was afraid of the risky bets and did not know what Tanvir held.

qa.q: What could Tanvir keep doing to protect trust with Siddharth?
qa.a: He could keep sharing his holdings, keep to the small limit for experiments, and keep his monthly review.

grounding: Four moments around money show envy of a friend's flaunted gains, a partner's fear, regret after a hidden loss and a creator's urgency tricks.

passage: Harish laughed along at Amandeep's joke about someone's caste, and the moment it was out, his stomach sank. That night he still felt bad, and the next day he told Amandeep, "That joke wasn't okay. I am sorry I laughed. I won't laugh at those again." At recess, some boys called Sachin names for his accent and said he could not join the cricket game because he was different. Harish's heart thumped, and he was afraid to disagree. He said nothing at first, but he sat down next to Sachin on the bench and shared his orange. When it happened again the next day, he told the class teacher. The teacher spoke to the whole class about names and gave every child the same turn to bat, whoever they were. Harish noticed that the teacher never treated a child differently because of home or language, and that made him feel safe. He picked Sachin for his team next.

qa.q: What did Harish share with Sachin on the bench?
qa.a: He shared his orange.

qa.q: How did Harish's response to Amandeep's joke differ from his response to the boys excluding Sachin?
qa.a: He laughed at the joke, felt guilty and apologised the next day, while with Sachin's exclusion he was afraid to speak at first but sat beside him and later told the class teacher.

qa.q: What was Harish feeling after laughing at the joke?
qa.a: He felt guilty; his stomach sank and he still felt bad that night.

qa.q: What could Harish keep doing to help Sachin?
qa.a: He could keep including Sachin, avoid jokes like that, and tell the teacher again if the name-calling continues.

grounding: A boy witnesses prejudice in different ways: his own guilty laugh, friends excluding a classmate, name-calling, and a teacher who treats everyone equally.

passage: Hansa admired her mentor Sonali from her first week and wrote down every remark, but she also asked hard questions, like "Why did you cut that section?" She knew Sonali was a person with flaws. In the early months Hansa asked Sonali to choose everything: the font, the tone of a client email, even which job to apply for. One day Sonali said, "What do you think?" and Hansa realised she was afraid of mistakes. She began deciding small things herself and asked Sonali for perspective rather than answers. Later Sonali began giving her personal errands and reports to write, then presented the work as her own. Hansa felt torn between loyalty and what was fair. "I would like my name on this report," she said, "and time to learn how you pitch." Sonali agreed for a month. As Hansa's designs won praise from clients, Sonali began to block her, moving Hansa's pitch slot and losing her file. Hansa was confused, but she kept thanking Sonali for what she had taught, found another guide, Kiran, at a different studio, and did not shrink her work to protect Sonali's pride.

qa.q: Who did Hansa turn to as another guide?
qa.a: She turned to Kiran, at a different studio.

qa.q: How did Hansa's way of asking Sonali for help change between the early months and later?
qa.a: In the early months she asked Sonali to choose everything, even which job to apply for, but after Sonali asked what she thought, she began deciding small things herself and asked for perspective rather than answers.

qa.q: What was Hansa feeling when Sonali began moving her pitch slot and losing her file?
qa.a: She was confused, since her designs were being praised while her mentor blocked her.

qa.q: What could Hansa do if Sonali's blocking continues?
qa.a: She could keep respecting what she was taught, keep seeking other guides like Kiran, and keep doing her best work instead of shrinking it.

grounding: A young designer's mentor relationship moves through admiration, over-dependence, exploitation and a mentor who feels threatened by her growth.

passage: Karthik touched the wall in fifth place at the inter-school swimming final, and the whole gallery saw it. Hemant, from the rival school, smirked. "Thought you were the champ." Karthik felt heat climb his neck, but he did not answer. He thought instead of his own last time, which he wanted to beat. His coach Bhavna's face fell as she looked at the timing board. He waited, then asked, "What can I learn from this?" She said, "Your turns cost you two seconds. Let's fix that." Her frown was not the end of anything. In the corridor his friend Sameer sat down beside him. "I still respect you," Sameer said, and Karthik's shoulders loosened. He accepted the comfort, and later brought Sameer tea when Sameer missed his selection. At home his mother did not scold. She hugged him and asked what had happened. He told her everything, and together they made a plan for extra turn practice.

qa.q: Where did Karthik place in the swimming final?
qa.a: He placed fifth.

qa.q: How did Hemant's reaction to Karthik's result differ from Sameer's, and how did Karthik respond to each?
qa.a: Hemant smirked and gloated, and Karthik stayed silent and thought about beating his own last time, while Sameer said he still respected him and Karthik accepted the comfort.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling when Bhavna's face fell at the timing board?
qa.a: He was probably uneasy and felt he had let her down, since he waited and then asked what he could learn.

qa.q: What could Karthik do next with the plan he made with his mother?
qa.a: He could follow the plan for extra turn practice and keep sharing honestly with her, as he did after the final.

grounding: After a public defeat, a swimmer meets a rival's gloating, a coach's disappointment, a friend's steady respect and a parent's comfort.

passage: Dilnaz waited by the door with the cake candles until the party ended and Harsha never came, though she had promised. Dilnaz's chest hurt. On Monday she did not snap or stay silent. "I felt sad when you didn't come. What happened?" she asked. Harsha said sorry; her cousins had arrived unexpectedly, and she had been too shy to call. Dilnaz forgave her, but remembered to be a little careful. It happened again with the school fair, then a sleepover, and again. Dilnaz stopped believing Harsha's big promises, though she still shared her snack and said hello every morning, and no longer counted on her for anything important. Then Dilnaz herself forgot the storybook she had promised Harsha two weeks running. Too embarrassed, she began to avoid Harsha in the corridor. By Thursday her stomach ached. She walked up. "I broke my promise. I am sorry. I will bring it tomorrow, and I will write myself a note so I don't forget." Harsha said, "Thanks for telling me," and they walked to class together.

qa.q: What had Dilnaz waited with by the door?
qa.a: She waited with the cake candles.

qa.q: How did Harsha explain missing the party, compared with how she responded when Dilnaz owned up about the storybook?
qa.a: Harsha said sorry and explained that her cousins had arrived unexpectedly and she had been too shy to call; when Dilnaz apologised for the storybook, Harsha said "Thanks for telling me" and they walked to class together.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling when she began to avoid Harsha in the corridor?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and ashamed of breaking her own promise, and her stomach ached by Thursday.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz do to make things right, and why did it work?
qa.a: She told Harsha the truth, said sorry and promised to bring the book tomorrow with a note, and an honest apology let them walk to class together.

grounding: One friendship around promises: hurt when a friend does not show up, forgiveness, distrust after repeated letdowns, and the shame of breaking one's own promise.
